_metadata.independence: I read only u17-blind-input.json; no other file, repository search, web lookup or external API was used.

hints.reason: Dragon reads as a serpent (serpentine Chinese dragons, 'the great serpent'); water is reached only through 'sea serpent' or 'water snake', one step removed.
Sea dragon (the real fish and the mythic sea dragon) reaches dragon; the sea is water.
Avatar: The Way of Water gives water; dragon arrives only via the dragon-like ikran/Toruk or the dragons of The Last Airbender, which needs explaining.

best_available.why: Sea dragon is a familiar creature name and sea is plainly water; the only hint that reaches both sides without a detour.

pairs.pair_note: One clean hint; SERPENT and AVATAR both lean on the water side being spelled out as 'sea'/'The Way of Water'.

hints.reason: Witches cast spells; nothing in 'spell' points at a dragon.
Both are stock figures of the fantasy genre; broad, but it reaches both words equally.
Maleficent is Disney's Sleeping Beauty witch/sorceress who turns into a dragon in the 1959 film (and whose raven becomes one in the 2014 film).

best_available.why: A single well-known story that contains both a witch and a dragon.

pairs.pair_note: MALEFICENT is the strong story route; FANTASY is a fair generic fallback; SPELL is witch-only.

hints.reason: Game of Thrones house sigils: the Targaryen dragon and the Stark direwolf; the word itself is GoT-coded.
Game of Thrones is the shared story: dragons for the Targaryens, direwolves for the Starks.
Both are beasts; a broad category word that nonetheless reaches both sides.

best_available.why: The most widely recognised route; names the show where dragon and wolf are the two famous house animals.

pairs.pair_note: All three pass; THRONES and SIGIL share the Game of Thrones route.

hints.reason: The phoenix is reborn in fire; the egg side rests on the phoenix being a bird or on the 'phoenix egg' fantasy trope rather than a scene most players hold.
Dragon eggs (Game of Thrones, fantasy generally) and fire-breathing dragons.
Frying an egg is immediate; fire is reached only as the heat under the pan or the sense of 'you'll fry'.

best_available.why: Both compounds (dragon egg, dragon fire) are familiar and equally strong.

pairs.pair_note: DRAGON carries the pair; PHOENIX and FRY each have one strong side.

hints.reason: Caviar is fish eggs by definition.
Fish spawn (lay eggs) and spawn is the mass of fish eggs itself.
Roe is fish eggs; a shorter, slightly less everyday word than caviar.

best_available.why: Everyone knows caviar is fish eggs.

pairs.pair_note: Three variants of the same fish-eggs route, all valid.

hints.reason: Ghosts are Halloween stock; egg is reached only through the egging prank, which players may not surface.
Egg white is a compound; the classic sheet ghost is white.

best_available.why: Egg white is a fixed compound and the white ghost is the default cartoon image.

pairs.pair_note: WHITE is a colour route but anchored by the compound 'egg white'; HALLOWEEN leans ghost-side.

hints.reason: Egg timer is a compound; glass arrives only because many egg timers are small sand-filled hourglasses.
Shared property: eggs and glass are the two archetypal fragile things.
Verb route: you crack an egg and you crack glass.

best_available.why: The same verb applies naturally to both.

pairs.pair_note: Two clean hints; TIMER is egg-first.

hints.reason: Yolk is part of the egg; gold is reached only through the yolk's golden colour.
The goose that laid the golden egg (Aesop; Jack and the Beanstalk).
Golden egg is a perfect phrase, but GOLDEN contains the target GOLD as a substring.

best_available.why: A universally known story that is literally about a golden egg.

pairs.pair_note: GOOSE is excellent; GOLDEN is a rule failure despite the obvious link.

hints.reason: Yolk is the egg's centre; nothing a player sees links yolk to heart without the cholesterol detour.
Eggs are the famous cholesterol food; cholesterol is the heart-health word.

best_available.why: The eggs-and-heart-health conversation is a shared cultural scene.

pairs.pair_note: CHOLESTEROL is the only real bridge; YOLK is egg-only.

hints.reason: Honey glaze is common; egg glaze (egg wash) is the baker's other glaze.
Eggs are the breakfast food; honey on toast, porridge or cereal is a recognisable breakfast item.

best_available.why: Both words are things you glaze with, so the hint is balanced rather than egg-first.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass at moderate strength; neither is a knockout.

hints.reason: Humpty Dumpty is the egg; 'all the king's horses' are in the same rhyme.
Humpty Dumpty is the egg; the rhyme's second half is 'all the king's horses and all the king's men'.

best_available.why: The more natural half of the name; the horses are in the rhyme everyone knows.

pairs.pair_note: Same route twice; horse side depends on recalling the rhyme's second line, so fairness is 1 not 2.

hints.reason: Eggshell is a compound; a 'shell of ice' exists but is not a familiar image.
Crack an egg; ice cracks / a crack in the ice.

best_available.why: Verb that applies vividly to both.

pairs.pair_note: CRACK is the pair; SHELL is egg-first.

hints.reason: Eggs are fried in a pan; the cast-iron pan.
Eggs in a skillet; 'cast-iron skillet' is almost a fixed phrase.

best_available.why: Cast-iron skillet is the tighter fixed phrase, and eggs are its signature dish.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass on the same cooking route.

hints.reason: Key lime is a compound; egg is reached only via key lime pie being made with yolks, which no player would see.
Easter egg is a compound; nothing links Easter to key.

best_available.why: If forced, LIME at least rests on a true two-sided fact (key lime pie uses egg yolks); EASTER has nothing on the key side.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Both hints are one-sided.

hints.reason: Fabergé eggs were made for the Russian tsars; tsar is a near-king, so the royal side is one small step.
Humpty Dumpty is the egg; 'all the king's horses and all the king's men' names the king outright.

best_available.why: The rhyme literally contains the word king.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; HUMPTY is the stronger.

hints.reason: Eggshell is immediate; reading a knight's armour as a 'shell' is an invented rescue.
Humpty Dumpty is the egg; knight only via 'all the king's men' standing in for knights (or the White Knight nearby in Through the Looking-Glass), a stretch.

best_available.why: The rhyme's king's men and the castle-wall setting give a weak but real medieval route; SHELL has none.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The pair lacks a natural bridge in the supplied hints.

hints.reason: 'Light and fluffy' is the stock description of scrambled eggs and omelettes; fluffy is a near-synonym for light in texture.
Candles give light; 'candling' an egg to check it is a real but niche farming term.
Egg incubator is immediate; light only via the heat-lamp bulb of a homemade incubator.

best_available.why: The phrase 'light and fluffy eggs' ties both words to one texture.

pairs.pair_note: FLUFFY passes on a shared-property route; the other two each have one weak side.

hints.reason: Lions live in zoos; nothing reaches egg.
A pride of lions; nothing reaches egg.

best_available.why: Neither works; ZOO is marginally less hopeless because zoos do display hatching eggs, but it remains one-sided.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Both hints are lion-only filler.

hints.reason: Shared shape: the moon is round and an egg is rounded (oval), a property route a player can see.
Mooncakes hold a salted egg yolk, but MOONCAKE contains the target MOON.
Full moon; nothing reaches egg.

best_available.why: The only hint that touches both sides, via shape.

pairs.pair_note: ROUND is a modest pass; MOONCAKE is a rule failure; FULL is moon-only.

hints.reason: Verb route: predators steal eggs and mice steal cheese, but neither side is a tight image for 'steal'.
Eggs sit in a nest; mice build nests.

best_available.why: A single everyday word that both words naturally own.

pairs.pair_note: NEST carries the pair.

hints.reason: Eggnog; nothing reaches night.
Night owl is a compound; owl reaches egg only as 'a bird that lays eggs'.

best_available.why: Night owl is a strong compound and an owl at least lays eggs; NOG has no night side at all.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: Finding Nemo is set in the ocean; Nemo is the lone surviving egg of the film's opening scene.
Sea turtles lay eggs on the beach and the hatchlings scramble into the ocean.

best_available.why: The turtle-egg-to-ocean scene is one of the most familiar nature images.

pairs.pair_note: TURTLE is strong; NEMO depends on remembering the egg opening.

hints.reason: Pirate treasure is immediate; egg only via the Easter egg hunt being a kind of treasure hunt.
The pirate's parrot; parrot reaches egg only as a bird that lays eggs.

best_available.why: Egg hunt as treasure hunt is a shared activity, a better egg route than 'birds lay eggs'.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Both hints are pirate-first.

hints.reason: Fabergé eggs were imperial gifts to the tsarina/empress and sit in royal collections; queen is one step from the royal luxury egg.
Alien franchise: the Alien Queen lays the eggs that hatch facehuggers.
Queen bee is a compound; the queen is the hive's egg-layer.

best_available.why: Queen bee is universal and her job of laying eggs is common knowledge.

pairs.pair_note: All three pass; FABERGE is the weakest queen link (tsarina, not queen).

hints.reason: Onion ring; egg only via the batter, which is not a route a player sees.
Egg yolk; nothing reaches ring.

best_available.why: Neither works; ONION at least has egg-and-onion as a familiar food pairing behind it, whereas YOLK has no ring side.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Two one-sided hints pointing opposite ways.

hints.reason: Pod loosely means an egg-like capsule and loosely evokes sci-fi machines (HAL's pod bay doors), but neither side is clear enough to follow.
EVE from WALL-E is the sleek egg-shaped robot; her egg silhouette is her signature design.

best_available.why: A well-known character whose whole look is 'egg-shaped robot'.

pairs.pair_note: EVE passes for anyone who has seen WALL-E; POD is vague on both sides.

hints.reason: Hard-boiled egg; rock hard.
Fossils are found in rock; fossilised dinosaur eggs are a familiar museum piece.
Dinosaur eggs are immediate; rock only via fossils being in rock.

best_available.why: Both compounds are everyday phrases.

pairs.pair_note: HARD is the clean pass; FOSSIL and DINOSAUR share one route with FOSSIL the better-balanced.

hints.reason: Eggshell; nothing reaches rose.
Easter egg is a compound; Easter is when Christ rose, reading ROSE as the past tense of rise (ordinary inflection).

best_available.why: The 'rose' verb reading is a real, well-known Easter phrase ('He rose again'), and Easter egg is a compound.

pairs.pair_note: EASTER passes only on the verb reading of ROSE; worth a second opinion if the owner wants the flower sense.

hints.reason: Boiled egg; nothing in 'boiled' points at salt.
Season with salt is near-synonymous; egg only as one of many things you season.
Salt and pepper is the fixed pair; egg only as the breakfast plate they are shaken over.

best_available.why: Salt-and-pepper-on-eggs is a real breakfast scene, giving the most recognisable egg side of the three.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The obvious shared scene (salting an egg) is not nailed by any supplied hint.

hints.reason: Candlelight throws shadows; egg only via the niche practice of candling eggs.
Eggshell; nothing reaches shadow.

best_available.why: The only hint with any egg side at all, even if candling is niche.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: Eggs hatch; most players do not associate sharks with hatching from eggs.
A 'mermaid's purse' is a shark egg case: a genuine two-sided link but niche natural-history knowledge.

best_available.why: The only hint whose connection actually involves both egg and shark, even though it is niche.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: A clutch of eggs; snake only as one of the animals that lays a clutch.
Eggs hatch; the baby snake breaking out of its egg is a familiar image, but 'hatch' alone does not point at snake over any other egg-layer.
Snakes swallow prey whole; the egg-eating snake swallowing an egg whole is a famous nature-documentary image, and 'swallow a raw egg' is a phrase in its own right.

best_available.why: The only hint where the snake side is strong and the egg side is a recognisable scene.

pairs.pair_note: SWALLOW passes; CLUTCH and HATCH are egg-first.

hints.reason: Charlotte's Web: Charlotte the spider's egg sac and her hatching children are the book's final act.
Egg sac is a compound and the spider's egg sac is its best-known instance.

best_available.why: Egg sac points straight at spiders.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass.

hints.reason: Sunny-side up egg; the sun is a star.
Star anise; egg only via Chinese tea eggs, which no player sees.
STARFISH contains the target STAR.

best_available.why: Sunny-side up is a universal egg phrase and sun-as-star is one step.

pairs.pair_note: SUNNY passes; STARFISH is a rule failure; ANISE is star-only.

hints.reason: Dining car; egg only as a thing one eats.
Egg carton; nothing reaches train.

best_available.why: Neither works; DINING at least sketches a breakfast-in-the-dining-car scene, whereas CARTON has no train side.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Two one-sided hints pointing opposite ways.

hints.reason: Poaching an egg is cooking it in water.
Boil an egg; boil water.
The egg float test (a bad egg floats, a fresh one sinks) and floating on water.

best_available.why: Poaching is specifically cooking an egg in water.

pairs.pair_note: All three pass; FLOAT depends on the freshness test.

hints.reason: Witches are Halloween stock; egg only through the egging prank.
Witch's cauldron; nothing reaches egg.

best_available.why: Egging houses is a real Halloween association; CAULDRON has no egg side.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: Hens lay eggs; wolf only as the predator at the henhouse, and the fixed phrase is 'fox in the henhouse'.
'Wolf down' is a phrasal verb; nothing in 'down' points at egg.

best_available.why: Predator-and-prey is a real if loose scene; DOWN is wolf-only.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: CAMPFIRE contains the target FIRE; cooking fish over a campfire would otherwise be a fair scene.
Grilling is cooking over fire; grilled fish is a staple.
Smoked fish (salmon, kippers); smoke comes from fire.

best_available.why: Equally direct on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Two passes; CAMPFIRE is a rule failure.

hints.reason: Where there's smoke there's fire; ghost only as a wispy, smoke-like apparition, a mood resemblance rather than a scene.
Campfire is a compound; ghost stories around the camp fire are the shared scene.
Spirit is a synonym for ghost; fire only via flammable spirits or 'fiery spirit'.

best_available.why: Campfire ghost stories put fire and ghost in one familiar scene.

pairs.pair_note: CAMP is the clean pass; SMOKE and SPIRIT each lean one way.
